title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', meaning automorphisms of the profinite genus-0 Teichmüller tower at level (0,3).

Objects. π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}: free profinite on loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ with one product relation. ρ is the order-3 automorphism cycling l_0→l_1→l_∞. σ_∞ is the involution exchanging l_0 and l_1, induced by z↦1−z, which fixes ∞. One studies the 'local' automorphisms u ∈ Aut_loc(Ĉ^+_{0,3}, σ_∞)'.

What the previous page did. It parametrized u by (g_0, γ) with h_0 = g_0^{-1}σ_∞(g_0). It then switched to the variable ζ = l_0^γ h_0. It assumed provisionally that π̂^{σ_∞} = 1 and that the Z/2-cocycle condition σ_∞(h_0)h_0 = 1 (67) is equivalent to h_0 being a coboundary.

This page.
- Rewriting (67) in terms of ζ gives the boxed (68): σ_∞(ζ) = l_1^γ ζ^{-1} l_0^γ.
- Summary: the relevant u correspond to pairs (ζ ∈ π̂_{0,3}, γ ∈ Ẑ) satisfying:
  - (a) 2γ+1 ∈ Ẑ^*;
  - (b) ζρ(ζ)ρ²(ζ) = 1;
  - (c) (68);
  - (d) 'liminary' conditions recovering (53), not conveniently expressible in ζ, γ.
- Redundancy (69): (ζ, γ) and (ζ', γ') give the same u iff γ = γ' and ζ' = l_0^{-α} ζ l_1^α for some α ∈ Ẑ.
- (70): the Z/3-cocycle condition (b) is solved parametrically. Either ζ = λρ(λ)^{-1} or ζ = λ l_0^{-1} ρ(λ)^{-1}, with λ ∈ π̂_{0,3}. Equation (68) then becomes an equation in λ (worked out on the next page).

Modern translation. Put x = l_0, y = l_1, m = γ, ζ = x^m f.
- Condition (68) becomes y^m f(y,x) = y^m f(x,y)^{-1}, i.e. the 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1.
- Condition (b) becomes x^m f(x,y) y^m f(y,z) z^m f(z,x) = 1, i.e. the hexagon (3-cycle) relation in an Ihara-type ordering.
- Condition (a) says λ = 2m+1 ∈ Ẑ^*.
- The redundancy (69), f ↦ x^{-α} f y^α, is exactly what the normalization f ∈ F̂_2' removes: its abelianization is (−α, α), so α is forced to be 0.
- Hence (a)–(c) modulo (69) are Drinfeld's relations (I), (II) defining GT^, before the pentagon. Condition (d) presumably carries the higher-level (pentagon-type) information.

The new step is reading (b) and (67)/(68) as nonabelian 1-cocycle conditions for Z/3 (via ρ) and Z/2 (via σ_∞), and parametrizing their solutions by coboundaries.
- The two classes in (70) are the two conjugacy classes of order-3 lifts of ρ in π̂ ⋊ Z/3. The quotient orbifold is a once-punctured sphere with two cone points of order 3, whose group is (Z/3 * Z/3)^.
- Abelianizing confirms the case split. M = Ẑ² with ρ satisfies M/(1−ρ)M ≅ Z/3, generated by e_0. The class of ζ is m mod 3.
  - m ≡ 0 gives the first case.
  - m ≡ −1 gives the second case (ζ ~ l_0^{-1}).
  - m ≡ 1 would force λ = 2m+1 ≡ 0 mod 3, which is excluded by (a).
- So the case is decided by λ ≡ ±1 mod 3, as the next page states ('p ≡ 1 ou −1 (3)').
errors: The second parametrization in (70) is a cocycle only under the right ordering convention for the product relation. Its norm is λ(l_0^{-1} l_1^{-1} l_∞^{-1})λ^{-1}, which needs l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1 rather than l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1. This is a convention issue, not a real error.

Exhaustiveness of (70) (nonabelian H^1(Z/3, π̂_{0,3}) has exactly two classes) is asserted without proof. Profinitely it needs a theorem on conjugacy of finite subgroups in profinite free products of finite groups (Herfort–Ribes type; Scheiderer's appendix to Lochak–Schneps). The analogous facts for Z/2 (π̂^{σ_∞} = 1 and (67) ⇔ coboundary) are explicitly 'admitted provisionally' on the previous page.
Condition (d) is left unformulated, so the description of u is incomplete as it stands.

ideas.what: Rewriting the Z/2 (2-cycle) relation and the Z/3 (hexagon) relation of the 'équation des lacets' as conditions on a single element ζ = l_0^γ f, with redundancy ζ ~ l_0^{-α} ζ l_1^α
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld/Ihara defining relations (I), (II) of GT^ (2-cycle and 3-cycle) in Ihara's ordering, with normalization f ∈ F̂_2'
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme suggests the program (GT tower, relations from the (0,3)/(0,4) levels) but not these explicit formulas

ideas.what: Interpreting the hexagon relation as a nonabelian 1-cocycle condition for Z/3 acting by ρ, and the 2-cycle relation as one for Z/2 acting by σ_∞, and parametrizing solutions as coboundaries λρ(λ)^{-1} or the twisted class λ l_0^{-1} ρ(λ)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Cohomological interpretation of GT^: f = g^{-1}θ(g) and analogous Z/3 statement, via conjugacy of torsion in profinite free products
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Lochak & L. Schneps, 'A cohomological interpretation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group', Invent. Math. 1997 (appendix by C. Scheiderer)

ideas.what: Two-case split of the Z/3 cocycle class according to λ = 2γ+1 ≡ ±1 mod 3 (explicit on the next page), forced by the abelianization H^1(Z/3, Ẑ²) = Z/3 together with invertibility of λ
ideas.modern_name: Dependence of the torsion conjugacy class on the cyclotomic character mod 3

missed.claim: Grothendieck already reformulates the 2-cycle and hexagon relations of the 'équation des lacets' (i.e. GT^ relations I, II) as Z/2 and Z/3 nonabelian cocycle equations. He solves them parametrically by coboundaries, with two Z/3 cases distinguished by λ mod 3. This anticipates the Lochak–Schneps cohomological interpretation of GT^ (1997) by over a decade.
missed.quote: La condition (64) peut encore se remplacer par une représentation paramétrique (70) ζ = λρ(λ)^{-1} ou ζ = λ l_0^{-1} ρ(λ)^{-1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority/attribution point in the GT literature. It shows the cocycle viewpoint and the role of torsion in the (0,3) orbifold group were part of Grothendieck's original program, not only of later reconstructions.

missed.claim: The 'conditions liminaires' (d), needed to recover (53) and presumably encoding the higher-level/pentagon compatibility, are flagged as not expressible conveniently in (ζ, γ). They are left open on this page.
missed.quote: Conditions liminaires pour retrouver (53) (qui ne s'exprimeront apparemment pas directement de façon commode en termes de ζ, γ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A cocycle-style formulation of the pentagon in the same variables (ζ or λ) would make the whole definition of GT^ cohomological. It is still not fully standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The algebra is short and correct, but it explicitly contains the Z/3 and Z/2 nonabelian-cocycle parametrization of GT^'s first two relations, including the λ mod 3 case split. In print this is credited to Lochak–Schneps (1997). It sits in apparently uncirculated notes.
transcription_corrections: The variable is ζ (as on the previous page), not ξ, throughout the page.
'Conditions limitrophes' should read 'Conditions liminaires' (cf. 'condition liminaire' on the previous page).
The parameter space is written π̂_{0,3} (ζ ∈ π̂_{0,3}), not Π̂^+_{0,3}.
Margin note reads roughly 'plutôt "équations en ζ" ou "en h_0"' (uncertain).
